why: In a script, a read before the script's own assignment of the name goes in text order (the user's ruling (step 11); MATLAB doc 'Function Precedence Order': a variable comes first, once there is one): `y = blend(1);` before `blend = 3;` calls `blend.m`, and the read after the assignment reads the variable. With the assignment moved first, no read is a call; moved back, the call again. In a loop, a read before the assignment in the loop's body calls `blend.m` on the first pass, a real call; and a read in the `else` of an `if` whose other clause makes the variable runs only when that clause did not, so it is a call too. Each step must end where a fresh index ends (project rule).
